newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures closed lower but well off their lows after a nervous session in which doubts about French and German ability to cut their deficits to levels needed to qualify for a single European currency weighed on prices.

The franc and PIBOR were struck by rumours, later disproven, that Germany's Bundesbank would raise its repo rate after its meeting. These rumours fuelled mark buying in Europe and knocked the franc down as low as 3.3821 per mark.
At 1500 GMT the franc was trading at 3.3798 per mark. Traders said volumes were not heavy.
The Bank of England's decision to raise official interest rates by 25 basis points to 6.75 percent left markets unmoved.

The worries about France's budget deficit were spurred by a series of newspaper reports which said that the French public deficit would be well above three percent this year and over four percent next year without corrective measures.

French daily La Tribune reported the deficit would be 3.6 to 3.7 percent of GDP this year, while Le Monde said former prime minister Alain Juppe had warned the new Socialist-led government it would have to take tough action to prevent the public deficit rising above four percent of gross domestic product next year.
Le Monde quoted Juppe as saying in a letter the deficit could still be reduced to three percent next year.

"The initial work on the budget outlook carried out by the budget ministry experts suggest a trend in public deficits to a figure above four percent of GDP, based, it is true, on particularly low forecasts for revenues," Le Monde quoted Juppe's letter as saying.
It said that Juppe had warned that economic growth was not having a strong enough effect on government and welfare revenues to allow the deficit to fall spontaneously.
Later in the session the mark rose after the Bundesbank left rates unchanged and Bundesbank officials said it was important to have a strong mark.

Analysts said markets did not react to a big jump in the current account surplus in April. They said that while the rise to 23.8 billion francs from 9.37 billion the month before was a sign of good exports, it also masked weak domestic demand and depressed imports.
Much of the bond future's fall was due to profit taking, dealers said and they added that each time the yield on the cash ten year bond approached 5.40 percent, sellers materialised.

Debt markets will focus on U.S. June producer prices due at 1230 GMT on Friday. A Reuter poll of U.S. economists predicted unchanged prices overall and a core rise of 0.1 percent after a 0.3 percent fall in both the overall and core indices in May.
French preliminary June consumer prices were due at 0645 GMT. They were not expected to have a significant impact on markets, dealers said.
